newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end the day stable at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares end the day stable at higher levels.

text.p: German IBIS DAX index ended the day stable, and higher, on Monday, with traders hesitant to take up any new positions in advance of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting in the United States.
The IBIS DAX index of 30 blue-chip German shares ended the day at 3,302.57 points, up 14.05 points or 0.43 percent, while June DAX DTB futures were up 11.5 points at 3,316.5.
Earlier the DAX index ended at 3,321.84 points, up 23.60 points or 0.72 percent.
The FOMC meeting, the policy-making unit of the U.S. Federal Reserve, could result in a rise in key interest rates.
However, many traders had taken this into account and built in a quarter percentage point rise into their trading strategy.
"The FOMC meeting is a good excuse not to trade today. Everyone is expecting a 25 basis point hike and is working on that basis," a Frankfurt broker said.

On the corporate side, the market was looking forward to Deutsche Bank AG and mixed utility Veba figures on Wednesday morning, when both hold their annual news conferences to announce details of their respective 1996 business years.

Two of the biggest gainers in afternoon trade were engineering groups Krupp-Hoesch, which ended up 17.50 marks, or 5.48 percent, at 337 marks, and Thyssen AG, which ended up 20 marks, or 5.12 percent, at 410.50 marks.
